title: Readings worth keeping
prompt: The climate model can cope with one missing measurement per reading, but not more. Write `solve(observations)` so it returns the readings with at least four of their five measurements, with the station code for "no value" turned into a real empty value.
rules: A measurement is missing when it's empty (null), NaN, or the code -9999. Keep readings where at least four are not missing.
In the rows you return, -9999 in those five columns becomes null. Every other value stays as it is, NaN included.
Return every column of `observations`, in order. Keep duplicates.
hints: `na.replace(-9999, None, subset=[...])` turns the code into null first.
`dropna(thresh=4, subset=[...])` keeps rows with at least four values present.
For number columns, `dropna` already treats NaN as missing.
starter:
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

MEASURES = ["temperature_c", "humidity_pct", "precipitation_mm", "wind_speed_kph", "pressure_hpa"]


def solve(observations):
    # Keep readings with at least four of the five measurements; -9999 becomes null.
    return observations
